Frequency and Time Reference Distribution Amplifiers The DIFS shall provide distribution amplifiers for the 10 MHz frequency reference and 1pps time reference signals. The distribution amplifiers shall accept the 10 MHz and 1pps signals at the DIFS external interfaces specified in Paragraphs 3.1.2.3.3.1 and Paragraph 3.1.2.3.3.2 and shall distribute the signals to all DIFS equipment requiring the reference signals at levels compatible with the DIFS equipment. The DMASS shall manage all DIFS equipment installed at the site and shall automate all tasks required to establish and maintain satellite communications DIFI paths traversing DIFS. Automation Functions The DMASS shall perform the following functions: Establish and terminate DIFI paths through DIFS based upon operator entered Satellite Access Agreement (SAA) parameters. Additional Safety Provisions Audible and visual warning devices shall be provided to indicate malfunctions and hazardous conditions that could cause injury and/or equipment damage. Audible warning signals shall be distinguishable from other sounds under normal operating conditions. Visual signals shall be readily visible and easily recognized. Colors of safety critical controls and indicators shall be yellow for caution and red for danger. Any color is permitted for functional controls or indicators, provided it is clear that safety is not involved. Safety warnings for proper operation and maintenance of all subsystems utilizing lasers shall be included in the technical manual. Safety warning labels shall be affixed near exit ports for all lasers exceeding Class 1 requirements as per ANSI Z136.1. All fiber optic systems shall comply with the safety and labeling requirements of ANSI Z136.2. The current legacy analog infrastructure limits scalability, resilience, and interoperability. Under this Call for Solutions, the selected vendor will deliver, integrate, install, and acceptance-test a flexible, open-standard, modular Digital IF solution across up to twenty (20) worldwide satellite communications (SATCOM) teleport sites. Increment 1 will establish a fully operational baseline designed to support subsequent capability upgrades and integrations in future fiscal years. SECTION 2 – REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION PROBLEM STATEMENT Area of Interest: Modular Digital Intermediate Frequency Solu

quires an open-standard Digital IF architecture. However, before committing to a full-scale global deployment, the DoW must validate the operation, interoperability, security, and performance of these modular commercial solutions in a rigorous representative environment. Technical Objective & Scope The DoW seeks a commercial solution for an Increment 1 Digital IF capability set built on a flexible, open standard (e.g., Digital Intermediate Frequency Interoperability compliant), modular architecture. The selected solution will undergo standard site acceptance testing and operational verification to confirm compliance with contract performance requirements and site compatibility. Upon successful acceptance, this operational configuration will serve as the standardized baseline for deployment and installation across up to twenty (20) worldwide SATCOM teleport sites. Mission Impact Successful validation and deployment of this flexible open-standard Digital IF architecture will directly enhance warfighter lethality and survivability by delivering a highly resilient, agile, and survivable GEO-SATCOM capability which rapidly adapts to contested/congested environments. Programmatic Objectives & Commercial Acquisition Strategy This acquisition is conducted under the Army Open Solutions (AOS) to identify and procure mature, commercially available technologies using Other Procurement, Army (OPA) funds. The Government's objective is to verify a c, followed by the immediate execution of priced contract options for the procurement, installation, and sustainment of production-ready subsystems at up to twenty (20) or more DoW Teleports and strategic gateway sites worldwide. Program Schedule and Milestones The offeror shall propose a streamlined schedule based on commercial product availability and rapid verification milestones: Commercial Solution Technical Demonstration Physical Configuration Audit (PCA) / Baseline Review First Article Delivery First Article Testing (FAT) & Verification Logistics & Performance Demonstration Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) and Teleport Integration SECTION 3 – SUBMISSION AND SELECTION Selection of awardee is planned to be conducted using a three (3) step approach: Step 1 – Request for Solution Briefs, Step 2 – Pitch Session and/or Vendor Technical Demonstration (PS/VTD) and Step 3 – Proposal Submission. A multi-disciplined working group of technical experts will evaluate the solution Briefs on their own technical merit and not against other solutions. Solution Briefs, and Pitches and/or Demos will be evaluated based on adherence to the following submission and evaluation criteria. Security Controls The DIFS shall incorporate technical security controls selected in accordance with CNSSI 1253 from NIST SP 800-53 as required for the security categorization specified in Paragraph 3.2.1.4.1. Note that the management, personnel, and operational controls required by CNSSI 1253 are also applicable to the DIFS but are non-technical in nature and therefore are not within the scope of this specification. Information Technology Products All Ethernet switches and other network components cybersecurity requirements will adhere to the vendor Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIG) program managed by the Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA). To meet cybersecurity requirements, all DIFS information technology products must comply with the DoD Security Requirements Guide for the product class. Products not covered by a STIG must enter the vendor STIG program.
